decision: Reuse and extend the existing Doré reader/ingestion core before introducing any parallel document conversion stack.

existingCore.capability: source-specific adapters normalize recognized corpus records into validated internal records with lossless ingestion checks

reuseFromExploration.EbookTranslatorCalibre: cache, batch and resume patterns only
reuseFromExploration.BabelEbook: paragraph alignment and bilingual rendering grammar only
reuseFromExploration.BabelDOC: PDF-specific fallback only if existing Doré adapters cannot produce a reliable normalized reading representation
reuseFromExploration.foliate-js: do not introduce as a second reader kernel unless a concrete unsupported EPUB requirement remains

extensionRule: Any missing PDF/EPUB/HTML/DOCX/TXT/IIIF capability should first be implemented as an adapter into the Doré normalized representation. Do not create format-specific translation pipelines.
translationBoundary: Translation consumes normalized segments, never raw file formats. Therefore translation logic is format-agnostic once ingestion succeeds.
bibleExclusion: Bible text, Bible translations, Hebrew/Greek Scripture witnesses and scripture-text records are rejected before translation provider invocation. Bible-world reference works may be handled separately according to product policy, but Scripture itself is hard-excluded.
benefit: Existing ingestion validation, provenance and source identity remain authoritative; new work is reduced to document adapters that are genuinely missing plus translation/cache/reader presentation.
next: Inventory all existing source/document adapters outside dore_core/readers and map them to the normalized representation before writing any new adapter.
